title: Philippine Landforms, Climate & Biodiversity

competencies.text: Explain unique landforms, climate, and life forms of the Philippines.

days.title: Unique Philippine Landforms
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will explain the unique landforms, climate and life forms of the Philippines using images, maps and cross-sections.

🏔️ Landforms and How They Formed

LandformHow it formedExample
VolcanoesMagma from subduction rising to the surfaceMayon, Taal, Kanlaon, Apo
Mountain rangesUplift and folding from plate collisionsCordillera Central, Sierra Madre
Karst (limestone) landscapesRainwater, a weak acid, dissolving uplifted limestoneChocolate Hills (Bohol), Puerto Princesa Underground River, El Nido
Valleys and plainsRivers depositing sedimentsCentral Luzon Plain, Cagayan Valley
Coral reefs and atollsCoral growth in warm, shallow, clear seasTubbataha Reefs
Human-made terracesCarved by Ifugao farmers on steep slopesBanaue Rice Terraces

🍫 The Chocolate Hills

More than 1,200 cone-shaped hills in Bohol are made of marine limestone that was uplifted and then shaped by rain and erosion over a very long time. They turn brown in the dry season — hence the name.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: What formed the Chocolate Hills of Bohol?

choices.label: Erosion of uplifted marine limestone
Lava cooling into small round domes
Ancient people piling soil into mounds
Meteorites striking the island long ago

scenario.explanation: Uplifted limestone from old sea floor was slowly dissolved and shaped by rainwater and erosion.

scenario.text: Which landform was created mainly by human activity?

choices.label: Banaue Rice Terraces
Mayon Volcano slopes
Sierra Madre range
Tubbataha Reefs atoll

scenario.explanation: The Ifugao people carved the terraces into mountainsides about 2,000 years ago or more.

scenario.text: How do karst landscapes such as underground rivers form?

choices.label: Weakly acidic water dissolves limestone
Lava tubes cool and harden into caves
Earthquakes crack granite into tunnels
Wind blows sand to carve deep caves

scenario.explanation: Rainwater with dissolved CO₂ is a weak acid that slowly dissolves limestone, forming caves and underground rivers.

days.title: Philippine Climate
days.content:
🌦️ A Tropical Maritime Climate

Being near the equator and surrounded by warm seas gives the Philippines high temperatures, high humidity and abundant rain. Two monsoon winds shape the seasons:

  • Amihan (northeast monsoon), about November to February — cooler, drier air in most of the west.
  • Habagat (southwest monsoon), about June to September — warm, moist air and heavy rain in the west.

The country also lies in the typhoon belt; about 20 tropical cyclones enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility each year.

📊 PAGASA's Four Climate Types (Modified Coronas)

TypeRainfall patternExample areas
ITwo pronounced seasons: dry Nov–Apr, wet the restWestern Luzon, Mindoro, Palawan, western Negros
IINo dry season; most rain Nov–JanCatanduanes, Eastern Samar, eastern Mindanao
IIISeasons not very pronounced; short dry periodCagayan Valley, parts of the Visayas
IVRain more or less evenly spread through the yearBatanes, parts of central Mindanao

Mountains matter: the side facing a monsoon gets heavy rain, while the sheltered side stays drier (a rain shadow).

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Uplifted limestone hills shaped by erosion
River flowing through a limestone cave
Southwest monsoon; heavy rain in the west
No dry season; heavy rain at year's end
Drier side of a mountain away from the wind
match.why: Moist air drops rain on the windward side.

days.title: Philippine Biodiversity
days.content:
🦅 A Megadiverse Country

The Philippines is one of about 17 megadiverse countries and also a biodiversity hotspot — very rich in species but heavily threatened. A large share of its land mammals, reptiles, amphibians and plants are endemic, meaning they live nowhere else on Earth.

SpeciesWhereStatus
Philippine EagleForests of Mindanao, Samar, Leyte, LuzonCritically endangered
TamarawOnly on MindoroCritically endangered
Philippine TarsierBohol, Samar, Leyte, MindanaoNear threatened
Visayan Warty PigNegros and Panay forestsCritically endangered

🏝️ Why So Many Unique Species?

  • Isolation: thousands of islands separated by deep water let populations evolve separately.
  • Varied habitats: mountains, lowland forests, mangroves, reefs and caves.
  • Warm, wet climate: supports rainforests and coral growth all year.
  • Coral Triangle: our seas are part of the world's richest marine region.

⚠️ Main Threat

The biggest threat is habitat loss — deforestation, conversion to farms and settlements, and reef destruction — followed by hunting, illegal wildlife trade, invasive species, pollution and climate change.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Connect landforms, climate and life. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: The tamaraw is found only on Mindoro. Which factor BEST explains this?

choices.label: Island isolation let it evolve separately
Mindoro is the coldest island in the country
Tamaraws can swim but dislike other islands
Mindoro has no mountains or any forests

scenario.explanation: Separated by deep water, Mindoro's animals evolved in isolation, producing species found nowhere else.

scenario.text: A farmer in Cagayan Valley (Type III) plans planting. What should he expect about rainfall?

choices.label: A short dry period; seasons not very distinct
No dry season at all, with constant heavy rain
Six months of complete drought every single year
Snowfall from December to February in the valley

scenario.explanation: Type III has a relatively short dry season, so farmers must still plan for a brief dry spell.

scenario.text: Eastern Samar gets heavy rain in December while western Luzon is dry. What BEST explains the difference?

choices.label: Amihan winds bring moisture to east-facing coasts
Habagat winds bring snow to Samar in December
Western Luzon is closer to the equator than Samar
Samar has more volcanoes that create rain clouds

scenario.explanation: The northeast monsoon (Amihan) carries moisture from the Pacific to eastern coasts, while the west lies in the dry season.

scenario.text: Why are the Philippines' coral reefs so rich in fish species?

choices.label: They lie in the warm, clear Coral Triangle
They are found in very cold and deep waters
They are protected from all sunlight and heat
They are fed by fresh water from many rivers

scenario.explanation: Warm, clear, shallow seas within the Coral Triangle support the highest marine diversity on Earth.

scenario.text: The Philippine Eagle population keeps declining. What is the MOST important action to protect it?

choices.label: Protect and restore large areas of its forest habitat
Feed the eagles chicken in city zoos every day
Move all the eagles to a colder foreign country
Build more roads through the eagle's mountain forests

scenario.explanation: Each eagle pair needs a large forest territory. Habitat loss is the main threat, so protecting forests matters most.

days.title: Connecting Land, Climate and Life
days.content:
🗺️ Reading Maps Together

Scientists overlay different maps to explain patterns:

  • A relief map shows mountains (Cordillera, Sierra Madre).
  • A climate map shows that the Sierra Madre's eastern side receives very heavy rain.
  • A forest and species map shows that these wet mountains still hold large forests with eagles and endemic frogs.

✂️ A Mountain Cross-Section

Imagine slicing through a mountain like Mt. Pulag from base to peak. As elevation rises, temperature drops: lowland rainforest → montane forest → mossy forest → grassland near the summit. Each zone has different plants and animals. This is why one mountain can hold many species.

🧠 Big Idea

Plate tectonics built our islands and mountains. Location and mountains shape our climate. Islands, mountains and climate together created the habitats where unique Filipino species evolved.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: How many climate types does PAGASA use for the Philippines?

choices.label: Four
Two
Three
Six

escape.explanation: PAGASA uses four climate types (I–IV) based on rainfall distribution.

escape.text: Which monsoon brings heavy rain to western Luzon from about June to September?

choices.label: Habagat (southwest monsoon)
Amihan (northeast monsoon)
Trade winds from the Pacific
Sea breeze from Manila Bay

escape.explanation: The southwest monsoon carries moist air from the West Philippine Sea, bringing heavy rain to the west.

choices.label: Found naturally in only one place
Found in every country on Earth
Extinct for more than a whole century
Brought in from another country

escape.explanation: Endemic species occur naturally in only one area — for example, the tamaraw on Mindoro.

choices.label: The richest marine region, including our seas
A triangle of hot deserts in central Mindanao
A mountain range in northern Luzon
A volcanic island chain near Japan

escape.explanation: The Coral Triangle covers parts of the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia and nearby countries and has the most coral and reef fish species.

escape.text: What is the MOST serious threat to Philippine biodiversity?

choices.label: Habitat loss from logging and reef damage
Too many protected areas being created each year
Animals moving into cooler forests
Too much rain on the mountain forests

escape.explanation: Losing forests and reefs removes the places species need to live — the leading cause of decline.

escape.text: Why does climbing Mt. Pulag take you through several forest types?

choices.label: Temperature drops as elevation increases
Soil becomes saltier near the summit
The mountain gets closer to the Sun
Rainfall stops completely above 1,000 meters

escape.explanation: Cooler temperatures at higher elevations support different plant communities, from rainforest to mossy forest to grassland.
